### Gandiva Projector and Filter API

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/gandiva/expr_projector_filter.rst

Code examples for creating and evaluating Gandiva Projectors and Filters.

```APIDOC
## Projector::Make

### Description
Creates a Projector instance that compiles expressions against a static schema for later evaluation on record batches.

### Method
Projector::Make

### Parameters
- **schema** (std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema>) - Required - The input schema of the record batches to be processed.
- **expressions** (std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Expression>>) - Required - The expressions to project.
- **projector** (std::shared_ptr<Projector>*) - Required - Output parameter that receives the created Projector.

### Returns
- **Status** - Indicates success or failure.

### Example
```cpp
std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema> input_schema = arrow::schema({field_x_raw});
std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema> output_schema = arrow::schema({field_result});
std::shared_ptr<Projector> projector;
Status status;
std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Expression>> expressions = {expression};
status = Projector::Make(input_schema, expressions, &projector);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
```
```

```APIDOC
## Filter::Make

### Description
Creates a Filter instance that compiles a condition against a static schema for later evaluation on record batches.

### Method
Filter::Make

### Parameters
- **schema** (std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema>) - Required - The input schema of the record batches to be processed.
- **condition** (std::shared_ptr<Condition>) - Required - The condition to filter on.
- **filter** (std::shared_ptr<Filter>*) - Required - Output parameter that receives the created Filter.

### Returns
- **Status** - Indicates success or failure.

### Example
```cpp
std::shared_ptr<Filter> filter;
status = Filter::Make(input_schema, condition, &filter);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
```
```

```APIDOC
## Projector::Evaluate

### Description
Evaluates the projector on a record batch, producing a vector of arrays that can be used to construct an output record batch.

### Method
Projector::Evaluate

### Parameters
- **batch** (const arrow::RecordBatch&) - Required - The input record batch to evaluate.
- **pool** (arrow::MemoryPool*) - Required - Memory pool used for allocations.
- **outputs** (arrow::ArrayVector*) - Required - Output parameter that receives the resulting arrays.

### Returns
- **Status** - Indicates success or failure.

### Example
```cpp
auto pool = arrow::default_memory_pool();
int num_records = 4;
arrow::Int32Builder builder;
int32_t values[4] = {1, 2, 3, 4};
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(builder.AppendValues(values, 4));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::shared_ptr<arrow::Array> array, builder.Finish());
auto in_batch = arrow::RecordBatch::Make(input_schema, num_records, {array});

arrow::ArrayVector outputs;
status = projector->Evaluate(*in_batch, pool, &outputs);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
std::shared_ptr<arrow::RecordBatch> result =
    arrow::RecordBatch::Make(output_schema, outputs[0]->length(), outputs);
```
```

```APIDOC
## Filter::Evaluate

### Description
Evaluates the filter on a record batch, producing a SelectionVector containing the indices that matched the condition.

### Method
Filter::Evaluate

### Parameters
- **batch** (const arrow::RecordBatch&) - Required - The input record batch to evaluate.
- **selection_vector** (std::shared_ptr<SelectionVector>) - Required - The selection vector to populate with matching indices. Must be initialized before calling.

### Returns
- **Status** - Indicates success or failure.

### Example
```cpp
std::shared_ptr<gandiva::SelectionVector> result_indices;
// Use 16-bit integers for indices. Result can be no longer than input size,
// so use batch num_rows as max_slots.
status = gandiva::SelectionVector::MakeInt16(/*max_slots=*/in_batch->num_rows(), pool,
                                             &result_indices);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
status = filter->Evaluate(*in_batch, result_indices);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
std::shared_ptr<arrow::Array> take_indices = result_indices->ToArray();
Datum maybe_batch;
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(maybe_batch,
                      arrow::compute::Take(Datum(in_batch), Datum(take_indices),
                                           TakeOptions::NoBoundsCheck()));
result = maybe_batch.record_batch();
```
```

```APIDOC
## Projector::Make (with SelectionVector mode)

### Description
Creates a Projector instance that is compiled for a specific SelectionVector mode, allowing projection with a selection vector.

### Method
Projector::Make

### Parameters
- **schema** (std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema>) - Required - The input schema of the record batches to be processed.
- **expressions** (std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Expression>>) - Required - The expressions to project.
- **selection_vector_mode** (SelectionVector::GetMode()) - Required - The mode of the selection vector to be used.
- **configuration** (ConfigurationBuilder::DefaultConfiguration()) - Required - Configuration for the projector.
- **projector** (std::shared_ptr<Projector>*) - Required - Output parameter that receives the created Projector.

### Returns
- **Status** - Indicates success or failure.

### Example
```cpp

status = Projector::Make(input_schema, expressions, result_indices->GetMode(),
                         ConfigurationBuilder::DefaultConfiguration(), &projector);
ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(status);
```
```

```APIDOC
## Projector::Evaluate (with SelectionVector)

Evaluates the projector on a record batch while applying a selection vector, producing a filtered output.

### Method

- **pool** (arrow::MemoryPool*) - Required - Memory pool used for allocations.

### Export int32 device array with release callback

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDeviceDataInterface.rst

Defines a release callback that frees CUDA resources and an export function that initializes an ArrowDeviceArray with a CUDA event for synchronization. The example uses CUDA but the pattern applies to any device.

```c
static void release_int32_device_array(struct ArrowArray* array) {
    assert(array->n_buffers == 2);
    // destroy the event
    cudaEvent_t* ev_ptr = (cudaEvent_t*)(array->private_data);
    cudaError_t status = cudaEventDestroy(*ev_ptr);
    assert(status == cudaSuccess);
    free(ev_ptr);

    // free the buffers and the buffers array
    status = cudaFree(array->buffers[1]);
    assert(status == cudaSuccess);
    free(array->buffers);

    // mark released
    array->release = NULL;
}

void export_int32_device_array(void* cudaAllocedPtr,
                               cudaStream_t stream,
                               int64_t length,
                               struct ArrowDeviceArray* array) {
    // get device id
    int device;
    cudaError_t status;
    status = cudaGetDevice(&device);
    assert(status == cudaSuccess);

    cudaEvent_t* ev_ptr = (cudaEvent_t*)malloc(sizeof(cudaEvent_t));
    assert(ev_ptr != NULL);
    status = cudaEventCreate(ev_ptr);
    assert(status == cudaSuccess);

    // record event on the stream, assuming that the passed in
    // stream is where the work to produce the data will be processing.
    status = cudaEventRecord(*ev_ptr, stream);
    assert(status == cudaSuccess);

    memset(array, 0, sizeof(struct ArrowDeviceArray));
    // initialize fields
    *array = (struct ArrowDeviceArray) {
        .array = (struct ArrowArray) {
            .length = length,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            // bookkeeping
            .release = &release_int32_device_array,
            // store the event pointer as private data in the array
            // so that we can access it in the release callback.
            .private_data = (void*)(ev_ptr),
        },
        .device_id = (int64_t)(device),
        .device_type = ARROW_DEVICE_CUDA,
        // pass the event pointer to the consumer
        .sync_event = (void*)(ev_ptr),
    };

    // allocate list of buffers
    array->array.buffers = (const void**)malloc(sizeof(void*) * array->array.n_buffers);
    assert(array->array.buffers != NULL);
    array->array.buffers[0] = NULL;
    array->array.buffers[1] = cudaAllocedPtr;
}

// calling the release callback should be done using the array member
// of the device array.
static void release_device_array_helper(struct ArrowDeviceArray* arr) {
    arr->array.release(&arr->array);
}
```

### Create Arrow arrays from JSON strings with ArrayFromJSONString helpers

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/arrays.rst

Shows how to create Arrow arrays from JSON strings using the helper functions ArrayFromJSONString, ChunkedArrayFromJSONString, and DictArrayFromJSONString. These helpers are intended for examples, tests, and quick prototyping, not for performance-critical code. The example covers simple types, timestamps, list, map, struct, chunked, and dictionary arrays.

```cpp
// Simple types
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto int32_array,
                      ArrayFromJSONString(arrow::int32(), "[1, 2, 3]"));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto float64_array,
                      ArrayFromJSONString(arrow::float64(), "[4.0, 5.0, 6.0]"));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto bool_array,
                      ArrayFromJSONString(arrow::boolean(), "[true, false, true]"));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto string_array,
    ArrayFromJSONString(arrow::utf8(), R"(["Hello", "World", null])"));

// Timestamps can be created from string representations
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto ts_array,
    ArrayFromJSONString(timestamp(arrow::TimeUnit::SECOND),
                        R"(["1970-01-01", "2000-02-29","3989-07-14","1900-02-28"])"));

// List, Map, Struct
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto list_array,
    ArrayFromJSONString(list(arrow::int64()),
                        "[[null], [], null, [4, 5, 6, 7, 8], [2, 3]]"));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto map_array,
    ArrayFromJSONString(map(arrow::utf8(), arrow::int32()),
                        R"([[["joe", 0], ["mark", null]], null, [["cap", 8]], []])"));
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto struct_array,
    ArrayFromJSONString(
        arrow::struct_({field("one", arrow::int32()), field("two", arrow::int32())}),
        "[[11, 22], null, [null, 33]]"));

// ChunkedArrayFromJSONString
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto chunked_array,
    ChunkedArrayFromJSONString(arrow::int32(), {"[5, 10]", "[null]", "[16]"}));

// DictArrayFromJSONString
ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    auto dict_array,
    DictArrayFromJSONString(dictionary(arrow::int32(), arrow::utf8()),
                            "[0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 3]", R"(["k1", "k2", "k3", "k4"])"));
```

```

### Create and concatenate ChunkedArray objects in R

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/chunked_array.Rd

Examples from the chunked_array Rd documentation showing how to create ChunkedArray objects in R. The first example passes separate vectors to create multiple chunks. The second shows that passing a list results in a single chunk. The third demonstrates type inference from the first chunk. The fourth shows concatenation of chunked arrays with c().

```r
# Pass items into chunked_array as separate objects to create chunks
class_scores <- chunked_array(c(87, 88, 89), c(94, 93, 92), c(71, 72, 73))
```

```r
# If you pass a list into chunked_array, you get a list of length 1
list_scores <- chunked_array(list(c(9.9, 9.6, 9.5), c(8.2, 8.3, 8.4), c(10.0, 9.9, 9.8)))
```

```r
# When constructing a ChunkedArray, the first chunk is used to infer type.
infer_type(chunked_array(c(1, 2, 3), c(5L, 6L, 7L)))
```

```r
# Concatenating chunked arrays returns a new chunked array containing all chunks
a <- chunked_array(c(1, 2), 3)
b <- chunked_array(c(4, 5), 6)
c(a, b)
```

### Run Query and Iterate Arrow C Stream Chunks

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CStreamInterface.rst

Implements a C consumer that fetches the schema, iterates over result chunks, and handles errors. Requires the database function from the previous example to populate the stream. On any error, it prints the stream's last error or the system error, releases the stream, and exits. It prints each chunk's row count and the total rows at the end, then releases the schema and stream.

```c
static void handle_error(int errcode, struct ArrowArrayStream* stream) {
   // Print stream error
   const char* errdesc = stream->get_last_error(stream);
   if (errdesc != NULL) {
      fputs(errdesc, stderr);
   } else {
      fputs(strerror(errcode), stderr);
   }
   // Release stream and abort
   stream->release(stream),
   exit(1);
}

void run_query() {
   struct ArrowArrayStream stream;
   struct ArrowSchema schema;
   struct ArrowArray chunk;
   int errcode;

   MyDB_Query("SELECT * FROM my_table", &stream);

   // Query result set schema
   errcode = stream.get_schema(&stream, &schema);
   if (errcode != 0) {
      handle_error(errcode, &stream);
   }

   int64_t num_rows = 0;

   // Iterate over results: loop until error or end of stream
   while ((errcode = stream.get_next(&stream, &chunk) == 0) &&
          chunk.release != NULL) {
      // Do something with chunk...
      fprintf(stderr, "Result chunk: got %lld rows\n", chunk.length);
      num_rows += chunk.length;

      // Release chunk
      chunk.release(&chunk);
   }

   // Was it an error?
   if (errcode != 0) {
      handle_error(errcode, &stream);
   }

   fprintf(stderr, "Result stream ended: total %lld rows\n", num_rows);

   // Release schema and stream
   schema.release(&schema);
   stream.release(&stream);
}
```

### List and read files from an S3 bucket with S3FileSystem

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/filesystems.rst

std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Expression>> expressions = {expression};

### DirectoryPartitioning$create()

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/Partitioning.Rd

Creates a DirectoryPartitioning object from a schema, defining how raw path segments are interpreted in order as partition variables.

```APIDOC
## DirectoryPartitioning$create()

### Description
Creates a DirectoryPartitioning object that interprets raw path segments in order according to the provided schema. For example, schema(year = int16(), month = int8()) defines partitions for file paths like "2019/01/file.parquet". NULL values in outer directories are skipped, and an error is raised if an outer directory is NULL and an inner directory is not.

### Method
DirectoryPartitioning$create()

### Parameters
- **schema** (Schema) - Required - A Schema object defining the partition columns and their types.

### Usage
DirectoryPartitioning$create(schema)

### Notes
- NULL values in path segments are skipped when writing and become NA when reading.
- An error is raised if an outer directory is NULL and an inner directory is not.
```

### Scan whole dataset with FileSystemDatasetFactory

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/dataset.rst

Creates a dataset from a base directory using FileSystemDatasetFactory, prints discovered fragments, and reads the entire dataset into a Table. Requires a filesystem, file format, and base directory; the factory scans the filesystem for files and infers the schema from the first file.

```cpp
// Read the whole dataset with the given format, without partitioning.
arrow::Result<std::shared_ptr<arrow::Table>> ScanWholeDataset(
    const std::shared_ptr<fs::FileSystem>& filesystem,
    const std::shared_ptr<ds::FileFormat>& format, const std::string& base_dir) {
  // Create a dataset by scanning the filesystem for files
  fs::FileSelector selector;
  selector.base_dir = base_dir;
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
      auto factory, ds::FileSystemDatasetFactory::Make(filesystem, selector, format,
                                                       ds::FileSystemFactoryOptions()));
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto dataset, factory->Finish());
  // Print out the fragments
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto fragments, dataset->GetFragments())
  for (const auto& fragment : fragments) {
    std::cout << "Found fragment: " << (*fragment)->ToString() << std::endl;
  }
  // Read the entire dataset as a Table
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto scan_builder, dataset->NewScan());
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto scanner, scan_builder->Finish());
  return scanner->ToTable();
}
```

### Construct struct array from existing arrays with StructArray.from_arrays

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/data.rst

Shows how to build a struct array from existing arrays using StructArray.from_arrays. Data storage is shared with the individual arrays, so no copy is involved. The example creates int16 and bool arrays, combines them with names 'x' and 'y', and prints the resulting type and array.

```python
>>> xs = pa.array([5, 6, 7], type=pa.int16())
>>> ys = pa.array([False, True, True])
>>> arr = pa.StructArray.from_arrays((xs, ys), names=('x', 'y'))
>>> arr.type
StructType(struct<x: int16, y: bool>)
>>> arr
<pyarrow.lib.StructArray object at ...>
-- is_valid: all not null
-- child 0 type: int16
  [
    5,
    6,
    7
  ]
-- child 1 type: bool
  [
    false,
    true,
    true
  ]
```

### Filter table with slicer (single condition)

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/ruby/README.md

Filter a table using a slicer. The example shows a greater-than condition and an in-range condition, with the resulting tables.

```ruby
table = Arrow::Table.new(
  'name' => ['Tom', 'Max', 'Kate'],
  'age' => [22, 23, 19]
)
table.slice { |slicer| slicer['age'] > 19 }
# => #<Arrow::Table:0x7fa38838c448 ptr=0x7fa3ad269f40>
#   name	age
# 0	Tom 	 22
# 1	Max 	 23

table.slice { |slicer| slicer['age'].in?(19..22) }
# => #<Arrow::Table:0x7fa3881cf998 ptr=0x7fa3a4bb5f30>
#   name	age
# 0	Tom 	 22
# 1	Kate	 19
```

### Build and submit source and binaries for a release candidate

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/developers/release.rst

Run these commands in order to build and submit source and binary artifacts for an Apache Arrow release candidate. Several steps require PMC membership and GitHub CLI; the binary upload step may need a GPG agent workaround on macOS. The crossbow status command uses the build ID printed by the submit step.

```default
# Waits for previous workflows to finish and uploads source and signatures to SVN.
#
# NOTE: This must be run by a PMC member
# NOTE: You need to have GitHub CLI installed to run this script.
dev/release/02-source.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Submit binary tasks using crossbow, the command will output the crossbow build id
dev/release/03-binary-submit.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Wait for the crossbow jobs to finish
archery crossbow status <crossbow-build-id>

# Download the produced binaries
# This will download packages generated from the archery tasks
# to a directory called packages/release-<version>-rc<rc-number>
dev/release/04-binary-download.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Sign and upload the binaries
#
# NOTE: This must be run by a PMC member
#
# On macOS the only way I could get this to work was running "echo "UPDATESTARTUPTTY" | gpg-connect-agent" before running this comment
# otherwise I got errors referencing "ioctl" errors.
dev/release/05-binary-upload.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Sign and upload MATLAB artifacts to the GitHub Releases area.
#
# NOTE: This must be run by a PMC member
# NOTE: You need to have GitHub CLI installed to run this script.
dev/release/06-matlab-upload.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Sign, build the installer for, and sign the installer for the FlightSQL
# ODBC Windows driver
#
# NOTE: This must be run by a PMC member
# Note: You need to have jsign installed and an available credential from
# ASF to sign artifacts. Not all PMC members will have access to code
# signing.
# Note: The script requires setup of ssl.com environment variables.
# Note: Invoking this script costs money.
dev/release/07-flightsqlodbc-upload.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Move the Release Candidate GitHub Release from draft to published state
# This will update the artifacts download URL which will be available for the
# verification step.
dev/release/08-publish-gh-release.sh <version> <rc-number>

# Start verifications for binaries and wheels
dev/release/09-binary-verify.sh <version> <rc-number>
```

### pq.write_table with Compression and Encoding Options

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/parquet/parquet.rst

Shows how to set compression and dictionary encoding options when writing Parquet files.

```APIDOC
## `pq.write_table` with Compression and Encoding Options

### Description
Controls compression and dictionary encoding when writing Parquet files. Supports various compression codecs and per-column settings.

### Method
`pq.write_table`

### Parameters
- **table** (Table) - Required - The table to write.
- **use_dictionary** (bool or list) - Optional - Whether to use dictionary encoding. Can be a boolean or a list of column names.
- **compression** (str or dict) - Optional - Compression codec. Can be a string (e.g., 'snappy', 'gzip', 'brotli', 'zstd', 'lz4', 'none') or a dictionary mapping column names to codecs.

### Example
```python
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', use_dictionary=False)
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='snappy')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='gzip')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='brotli')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='zstd')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='lz4')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression='none')
>>> pq.write_table(table, 'example.parquet', compression={'one': 'snappy', 'two': 'gzip'},
...                use_dictionary=['one', 'two'])
```
```

### Write and read Feather dataset with Dataset API

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/dataset.rst

Shows how to write a Feather dataset and then read it back using the Dataset API. The first block creates two Feather files with arrow::ipc::MakeFileWriter, and the second block demonstrates constructing a FileSystemDatasetFactory with a format object (here ParquetFileFormat, but the text says to pass IpcFileFormat for Feather).

```cpp
// Set up a dataset by writing two Feather files.
arrow::Result<std::string> CreateExampleFeatherDataset(
    const std::shared_ptr<fs::FileSystem>& filesystem, const std::string& root_path) {
  auto base_path = root_path + "/feather_dataset";
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(filesystem->CreateDir(base_path));
  // Create an Arrow Table
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto table, CreateTable());
  // Write it into two Feather files
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto output,
                        filesystem->OpenOutputStream(base_path + "/data1.feather"));
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto writer,
                        arrow::ipc::MakeFileWriter(output.get(), table->schema()));
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->WriteTable(*table->Slice(0, 5)));
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->Close());
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(output,
                        filesystem->OpenOutputStream(base_path + "/data2.feather"));
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(writer,
                        arrow::ipc::MakeFileWriter(output.get(), table->schema()));
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->WriteTable(*table->Slice(5)));
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->Close());
  return base_path;
}
```

```cpp
auto format = std::make_shared<ds::ParquetFileFormat>();
// ...
auto factory = ds::FileSystemDatasetFactory::Make(filesystem, selector, format, options)
                   .ValueOrDie();
```

# dev/release/post-08-docs.sh 10.0.0 9.0.0
dev/release/post-08-docs.sh X.Y.Z PREVIOUS_X.PREVIOUS_Y.PREVIOUS_Z

### Building a Buffer with arrow::BufferBuilder

```cpp
BufferBuilder builder;
builder.Resize(11);  // reserve enough space for 11 bytes
builder.Append("hello ", 6);
builder.Append("world", 5);

auto maybe_buffer = builder.Finish();
if (!maybe_buffer.ok()) {
   // ... handle buffer allocation error
}
std::shared_ptr<arrow::Buffer> buffer = *maybe_buffer;
```

### show_exec_plan(x)

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/show_exec_plan.Rd

Prints the execution plan details for an arrow_dplyr_query object. It returns the input object invisibly.

```APIDOC
## show_exec_plan(x)

### Description
Shows the details of an Arrow Execution Plan for an `arrow_dplyr_query` object.

### Usage
```r
show_exec_plan(x)
```

### Arguments
- **x** (`arrow_dplyr_query`) - Required - An `arrow_dplyr_query` to print the `ExecPlan` for.

### Value
Returns `x`, invisibly.

### Details
This function gives more details about the logical query plan that will be executed when evaluating an `arrow_dplyr_query` object. It calls the C++ `ExecPlan` object's print method. Functionally, it is similar to `dplyr::explain()`. This function is used as the `dplyr::explain()` and `dplyr::show_query()` methods.

### Examples
```r
library(dplyr)
mtcars |>
  arrow_table() |>
  filter(mpg > 20) |>
  mutate(x = gear / carb) |>
  show_exec_plan()
```
```

--------------------------------

### Define a custom SinkNodeConsumer and use consuming_sink

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/acero/user_guide.rst

Shows how to define a custom SinkNodeConsumer that counts batches and returns a finish future, then create a consuming_sink node and run the plan to completion. The plan has no output; data is consumed within the plan.

```cpp
// define a Custom SinkNodeConsumer
std::atomic<uint32_t> batches_seen{0};
arrow::Future<> finish = arrow::Future<>::Make();
struct CustomSinkNodeConsumer : public cp::SinkNodeConsumer {

    CustomSinkNodeConsumer(std::atomic<uint32_t> *batches_seen, arrow::Future<>finish):
    batches_seen(batches_seen), finish(std::move(finish)) {}
    // Consumption logic can be written here
    arrow::Status Consume(cp::ExecBatch batch) override {
    // data can be consumed in the expected way
    // transfer to another system or just do some work
    // and write to disk
    (*batches_seen)++;
    return arrow::Status::OK();
    }

    arrow::Future<> Finish() override { return finish; }

    std::atomic<uint32_t> *batches_seen;
    arrow::Future<> finish;

};

std::shared_ptr<CustomSinkNodeConsumer> consumer =
        std::make_shared<CustomSinkNodeConsumer>(&batches_seen, finish);

arrow::acero::ExecNode *consuming_sink;

ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(consuming_sink, MakeExecNode("consuming_sink", plan.get(),
    {source}, cp::ConsumingSinkNodeOptions(consumer)));
```

```cpp
/// \brief An example showing a consuming sink node
///
/// Source-Consuming-Sink
/// This example shows how the data can be consumed within the execution plan
/// by using a ConsumingSink node. There is no data output from this execution plan.
arrow::Status SourceConsumingSinkExample() {
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto basic_data, MakeBasicBatches());

  auto source_node_options = ac::SourceNodeOptions{basic_data.schema, basic_data.gen()};

  ac::Declaration source{"source", std::move(source_node_options)};

  std::atomic<uint32_t> batches_seen{0};
  arrow::Future<> finish = arrow::Future<>::Make();
  struct CustomSinkNodeConsumer : public ac::SinkNodeConsumer {
    CustomSinkNodeConsumer(std::atomic<uint32_t>* batches_seen, arrow::Future<> finish)
        : batches_seen(batches_seen), finish(std::move(finish)) {}

    arrow::Status Init(const std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema>& schema,
                       ac::BackpressureControl* backpressure_control,
                       ac::ExecPlan* plan) override {
      // This will be called as the plan is started (before the first call to Consume)
      // and provides the schema of the data coming into the node, controls for pausing /
      // resuming input, and a pointer to the plan itself which can be used to access
      // other utilities such as the thread indexer or async task scheduler.
      return arrow::Status::OK();
    }

    arrow::Status Consume(cp::ExecBatch batch) override {
      (*batches_seen)++;
      return arrow::Status::OK();
    }

    arrow::Future<> Finish() override {
      // Here you can perform whatever (possibly async) cleanup is needed, e.g. closing
      // output file handles and flushing remaining work
      return arrow::Future<>::MakeFinished();
    }

    std::atomic<uint32_t>* batches_seen;
    arrow::Future<> finish;
  };
  std::shared_ptr<CustomSinkNodeConsumer> consumer =
      std::make_shared<CustomSinkNodeConsumer>(&batches_seen, finish);

  ac::Declaration consuming_sink{"consuming_sink",
                                 {std::move(source)},
                                 ac::ConsumingSinkNodeOptions(std::move(consumer))};

  // Since we are consuming the data within the plan there is no output and we simply
  // run the plan to completion instead of collecting into a table.
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(ac::DeclarationToStatus(std::move(consuming_sink)));

  std::cout << "The consuming sink node saw " << batches_seen.load() << " batches"
            << std::endl;
  return arrow::Status::OK();
}
```

### Build a RecordBatch with arrow::RecordBatch::Make

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/tutorials/basic_arrow.rst

Builds a RecordBatch from a Schema, a shared column length (days->length()), and three Arrays (days, months, years). The length must match across all columns. Outputs the batch contents with ToString().

```cpp
  // With the schema and Arrays full of data, we can make our RecordBatch! Here,
  // each column is internally contiguous. This is in opposition to Tables, which we'll
  // see next.
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::RecordBatch> rbatch;
  // The RecordBatch needs the schema, length for columns, which all must match,
  // and the actual data itself.
  rbatch = arrow::RecordBatch::Make(schema, days->length(), {days, months, years});

  std::cout << rbatch->ToString();
```

cimport cpython

cdef ArrowSchema* get_arrow_schema_py_capsule(object capsule) except NULL:
    return <ArrowSchema*>cpython.PyCapsule_GetPointer(capsule, 'arrow_schema')

### Create CsvFileFormat with null_values and readr-style na options

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/CsvFileFormat.Rd

Creates a temporary directory with a CSV file, then demonstrates two ways to create a CsvFileFormat object: using Arrow-style convert_options with null_values and using readr-style na option. Both are passed to open_dataset().

```r
# Set up directory for examples
tf <- tempfile()
dir.create(tf)
on.exit(unlink(tf))
df <- data.frame(x = c("1", "2", "NULL"))
write.table(df, file.path(tf, "file1.txt"), sep = ",", row.names = FALSE)

# Create CsvFileFormat object with Arrow-style null_values option
format <- CsvFileFormat$create(convert_options = list(null_values = c("", "NA", "NULL")))
open_dataset(tf, format = format)

# Use readr-style options
format <- CsvFileFormat$create(na = c("", "NA", "NULL"))
open_dataset(tf, format = format)
```

### Configure Maven toolchains.xml for a JDK

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/developers/java/building.rst

Add this snippet to the Maven toolchains.xml file (usually under ${HOME}/.m2) to register a JDK for testing. Replace the version, vendor, and jdkHome values with the corresponding JDK details.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF8"?>
<toolchains>

  [...]

  <toolchain>
    <type>jdk</type>
    <provides>
      <version>21</version> <!-- Replace with the corresponding JDK version: 11, 17, ... -->
      <vendor>temurin</vendor> <!-- Replace with the vendor/distribution: temurin, oracle, zulu ... -->
    </provides>
    <configuration>
      <jdkHome>path/to/jdk/home</jdkHome> <!-- Replace with the path to the JDK -->
    </configuration>
  </toolchain>

  [...]

</toolchains>
```

### Use ArrowCUDA::DeviceManager and Buffer

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/ruby/red-arrow-cuda/README.md

Shows how to use Red Arrow CUDA to create a GPU buffer, write data to it, and copy the data back to the host. Raises an error if no GPU is found.

```ruby
require "arrow-cuda"

manager = ArrowCUDA::DeviceManager.new
if manager.n_devices.zero?
  raise "No GPU is found"
end

context = manager[0]
buffer = ArrowCUDA::Buffer.new(context, 128)
ArrowCUDA::BufferOutputStream.open(buffer) do |stream|
  stream.write("Hello World")
end
puts buffer.copy_to_host(0, 11) # => "Hello World"
```

### ArrowDeviceArrayStream

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDeviceDataInterface.rst

The ArrowDeviceArrayStream structure defines the C device stream interface. It includes a device type and callbacks for schema retrieval, getting the next data chunk, error handling, and release.

```APIDOC
## ArrowDeviceArrayStream

### Description
The ArrowDeviceArrayStream structure is the core of the C Device Stream Interface. It provides a streaming source of Arrow data chunks, all with the same schema and accessible from a specified device type. Consumers interact with the stream through its callbacks.

### Structure Definition
```c
struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream {
    // device type that all arrays will be accessible from
    ArrowDeviceType device_type;
    // callbacks
    int (*get_schema)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*, struct ArrowSchema*);
    int (*get_next)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*, struct ArrowDeviceArray*);
    const char* (*get_last_error)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*);

    // release callback
    void (*release)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*);

    // opaque producer-specific data
    void* private_data;
};
```

### Fields

#### device_type
- **Type**: ArrowDeviceType
- **Mandatory**: Yes
- **Description**: The device type that this stream produces data on. All ArrowDeviceArrays produced by this stream should have the same device type as set here.

#### get_schema
- **Type**: int (*)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*, struct ArrowSchema*)
- **Mandatory**: Yes
- **Description**: Callback to query the schema of the chunks in the stream. The schema is the same for all data chunks. Must NOT be called on a released stream.
- **Return value**: 0 on success, non-zero error code otherwise.

#### get_next
- **Type**: int (*)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*, struct ArrowDeviceArray*)
- **Mandatory**: Yes
- **Description**: Callback to get the next chunk of data in the stream. The next chunk MUST be accessible from a device type matching the stream's device_type. Must NOT be called on a released stream.
- **Return value**: 0 on success, non-zero error code otherwise. On success, check if the embedded ArrowArray is released to determine end of stream.

#### get_last_error
- **Type**: const char* (*)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*)
- **Mandatory**: Yes
- **Description**: Callback to get a textual description of the last error. Must ONLY be called if the last operation returned an error. Must NOT be called on a released stream.
- **Return value**: Pointer to a NULL-terminated UTF-8 string, or NULL if no description available. The pointer is valid only until the next call of any stream callback.

#### release
- **Type**: void (*)(struct ArrowDeviceArrayStream*)
- **Mandatory**: Yes
- **Description**: Producer-provided release callback to free resources associated with the stream.

### Usage Notes
- The canonical guard `ARROW_C_DEVICE_STREAM_INTERFACE` prevents duplicate definitions when copied.
- All chunks in a stream must have the same schema and device type.
- If multiple device types are needed, separate stream objects should be provided.
```

### Create a Table with two int32 columns

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/tutorials/compute_tutorial.rst

Builds a Table with two int32 columns (A and B) using Int32Builder, initializes the compute module, and creates the table with 5 rows.

```cpp
  // Create a couple 32-bit integer arrays.
  arrow::Int32Builder int32builder;
  int32_t some_nums_raw[5] = {34, 624, 2223, 5654, 4356};
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(int32builder.AppendValues(some_nums_raw, 5));
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Array> some_nums;
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(some_nums, int32builder.Finish());

  int32_t more_nums_raw[5] = {75342, 23, 64, 17, 736};
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(int32builder.AppendValues(more_nums_raw, 5));
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Array> more_nums;
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(more_nums, int32builder.Finish());

  // Make a table out of our pair of arrays.
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Field> field_a, field_b;
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema> schema;

  field_a = arrow::field("A", arrow::int32());
  field_b = arrow::field("B", arrow::int32());

  schema = arrow::schema({field_a, field_b});

  // Initialize the compute module to register the required compute kernels.
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(arrow::compute::Initialize());

  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Table> table;
  table = arrow::Table::Make(schema, {some_nums, more_nums}, 5);
```

### Access Int64Array contents

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/arrays.rst

Accesses the contents of an arrow::Int64Array after casting from arrow::Array. Shows how to get the null bitmap and raw values, and how to query null status and value at a given index.

```cpp
// Cast the Array to its actual type to access its data
auto int64_array = std::static_pointer_cast<arrow::Int64Array>(array);

// Get the pointer to the null bitmap
const uint8_t* null_bitmap = int64_array->null_bitmap_data();

// Get the pointer to the actual data
const int64_t* data = int64_array->raw_values();

// Alternatively, given an array index, query its null bit and value directly
int64_t index = 2;
if (!int64_array->IsNull(index)) {
   int64_t value = int64_array->Value(index);
}
```

### Filter and select columns from a dataset

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/dataset.rst

Creates a dataset from a filesystem directory and scans it to select only column "b" and rows where b < 4. Uses FileSystemDatasetFactory, NewScan, Project, and Filter with a compute expression. The column selection is pushed down where possible to reduce work.

```cpp
arrow::Result<std::shared_ptr<arrow::Table>> FilterAndSelectDataset(
    const std::shared_ptr<fs::FileSystem>& filesystem,
    const std::shared_ptr<ds::FileFormat>& format, const std::string& base_dir) {
  fs::FileSelector selector;
  selector.base_dir = base_dir;
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
      auto factory, ds::FileSystemDatasetFactory::Make(filesystem, selector, format,
                                                       ds::FileSystemFactoryOptions()));
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto dataset, factory->Finish());
  // Read specified columns with a row filter
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto scan_builder, dataset->NewScan());
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(scan_builder->Project({"b"}));
  ARROW_RETURN_NOT_OK(scan_builder->Filter(cp::less(cp::field_ref("b"), cp::literal(4))));
  ARROW_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(auto scanner, scan_builder->Finish());
  return scanner->ToTable();
}
```

### Iterate record batches with RecordBatchReader

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/data.rst

Shows how to create a RecordBatchReader from a generator of record batches and iterate over them.

```python
>>> schema = pa.schema([('x', pa.int64())])
>>>
>>> def iter_record_batches():
...    for i in range(2):
...       yield pa.RecordBatch.from_arrays([pa.array([1, 2, 3])], schema=schema)
>>>
>>> reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_batches(schema, iter_record_batches())
>>> print(reader.schema)
x: int64
>>> for batch in reader:
...    print(batch)
pyarrow.RecordBatch
x: int64
----
x: [1,2,3]
pyarrow.RecordBatch
x: int64
----
x: [1,2,3]
```

driver={Apache Arrow Flight SQL ODBC Driver};host=127.0.0.1;port=12345;uid=sample_user;pwd=sample_password;useEncryption=false;useWideChar=true;
```

### Minimal CMakeLists.txt to link Arrow shared library

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/build_system.rst

Use this CMakeLists.txt to compile a source file into an executable linked with the Arrow C++ shared library. Requires CMake 3.25 or higher and an installed Arrow package.

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)

project(MyExample)

find_package(Arrow REQUIRED)

add_executable(my_example my_example.cc)
target_link_libraries(my_example PRIVATE Arrow::arrow_shared)
```

### Error for Dataset queries with unsupported expressions

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/vignettes/data_wrangling.Rmd

For Dataset objects, arrow raises an error when it detects unsupported expressions. This example writes the starwars data to disk, opens it as a Dataset, and then runs the same pipeline, resulting in an error.

```R
# write and open starwars dataset
dataset_path <- tempfile()
write_dataset(starwars, dataset_path)
sw2 <- open_dataset(dataset_path)

# dplyr pipeline with unsupported expressions
sw2 |>
  filter(!is.na(height), !is.na(mass)) |>
  transmute(name, height, mass, res = residuals(lm(mass ~ height)))
```

### Convert DuckDB result to Arrow and collect

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/to_arrow.Rd

Example pipeline using to_arrow() after a DuckDB query. The result of to_arrow() can only be collected or computed once, so use collect() as the final step or call as_arrow_table() to materialize the table in memory.

```r
library(dplyr)

ds <- InMemoryDataset$create(mtcars)

ds |>
  filter(mpg < 30) |>
  to_duckdb() |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarize(mean_mpg = mean(mpg, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  to_arrow() |>
  collect()
```

### Write multiple row groups with ParquetWriter

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/parquet/parquet.rst

Shows how to write a Parquet file with multiple row groups using ParquetWriter. The example writes the same table three times and then verifies the number of row groups is 3.

```python
>>> with pq.ParquetWriter('example2.parquet', table.schema) as writer:
...     for i in range(3):
...         writer.write_table(table)
>>> pf2 = pq.ParquetFile('example2.parquet')
>>> pf2.num_row_groups
3
```

### Extract an Arrow Field from a Schema by index

### Create UUID scalar and array with type inference

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/extending_types.rst

Shows how PyArrow infers the UUID type from Python's uuid.UUID objects. The example creates a scalar and an array from a list of UUIDs, and prints the inferred type.

```python
>>> import uuid
>>> import pyarrow as pa

>>> pa.scalar(uuid.uuid4())
<pyarrow.UuidScalar: UUID('...')>

>>> uuids = [uuid.uuid4() for _ in range(3)]
>>> arr = pa.array(uuids)
>>> arr.type
UuidType(extension<arrow.uuid>)
```

### open_dataset(sources, schema, partitioning, hive_style, unify_schemas, format, factory_options, ...)

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/open_dataset.Rd

Opens a multi-file dataset from a directory, file paths, or existing Dataset objects. Supports schema inference, partitioning, and various file formats.

```APIDOC
## open_dataset(sources, schema, partitioning, hive_style, unify_schemas, format, factory_options, ...)

### Description
Opens a multi-file dataset from a directory, file paths, or existing Dataset objects. Supports schema inference, partitioning, and various file formats.

### Method
Function call

### Endpoint
open_dataset(sources, schema = NULL, partitioning = hive_partition(), hive_style = NA, unify_schemas = NULL, format = c("parquet", "arrow", "ipc", "feather", "csv", "tsv", "text", "json"), factory_options = list(), ...)

### Parameters
#### sources
- **sources** (string path/URI, FileSystem, character vector, list of Dataset, list of DatasetFactory) - Required - One of: a string path or URI to a directory containing data files; a FileSystem that references a directory containing data files; a string path or URI to a single file; a character vector of paths or URIs to individual data files; a list of Dataset objects as created by this function; a list of DatasetFactory objects as created by dataset_factory(). When sources is a vector of file URIs, they must all use the same protocol and point to files located in the same file system and having the same format.

#### schema
- **schema** (Schema) - Optional - Schema for the Dataset. If NULL (the default), the schema will be inferred from the data sources.

#### partitioning
- **partitioning** (Schema, character vector, Partitioning, PartitioningFactory, NULL) - Optional - When sources is a directory path/URI, one of: a Schema, in which case the file paths relative to sources will be parsed, and path segments will be matched with the schema fields; a character vector that defines the field names corresponding to those path segments (that is, you're providing the names that would correspond to a Schema but the types will be autodetected); a Partitioning or PartitioningFactory, such as returned by hive_partition(); NULL for no partitioning. The default is to autodetect Hive-style partitions unless hive_style = FALSE. When sources is not a directory path/URI, partitioning is ignored.

#### hive_style
- **hive_style** (logical) - Optional - Logical: should partitioning be interpreted as Hive-style? Default is NA, which means to inspect the file paths for Hive-style partitioning and behave accordingly.

#### unify_schemas
- **unify_schemas** (logical) - Optional - logical: should all data fragments (files, Datasets) be scanned in order to create a unified schema from them? If FALSE, only the first fragment will be inspected for its schema. Use this fast path when you know and trust that all fragments have an identical schema. The default is FALSE when creating a dataset from a directory path/URI or vector of file paths/URIs (because there may be many files and scanning may be slow) but TRUE when sources is a list of Datasets (because there should be few Datasets in the list and their Schemas are already in memory).

#### format
- **format** (FileFormat object or string) - Optional - A FileFormat object, or a string identifier of the format of the files in x. This argument is ignored when sources is a list of Dataset objects. Currently supported values: "parquet", "ipc"/"arrow" for the Arrow IPC format (also supported as "feather" but this is deprecated), "csv"/"text", aliases for the same thing (because comma is the default delimiter for text files), "tsv", equivalent to passing format = "text", delimiter = "\\t", "json", for JSON format datasets. Note: only newline-delimited JSON (aka ND-JSON) datasets are currently supported. Default is "parquet", unless a delimiter is also specified, in which case it is assumed to be "text".

#### factory_options
- **factory_options** (list) - Optional - list of optional FileSystemFactoryOptions: partition_base_dir: string path segment prefix to ignore when discovering partition information with DirectoryPartitioning. Not meaningful (ignored with a warning) for HivePartitioning, nor is it valid when providing a vector of file paths. exclude_invalid_files: logical: should files that are not valid data files be excluded? Default is FALSE because checking all files up front incurs I/O and thus will be slower, especially on remote filesystems. If false and there are invalid files, there will be an error at scan time. This is the only FileSystemFactoryOption that is valid for both when providing a directory path in which to discover files and when providing a vector of file paths. selector_ignore_prefixes: character vector of file prefixes to ignore when discovering files in a directory. If invalid files can be excluded by a common filename prefix this way, you can avoid the I/O cost of exclude_invalid_files. Not valid when providing a vector of file paths (but if you're providing the file list, you can filter invalid files yourself).

#### ...
- **...** (additional arguments) - Optional - Additional arguments passed to the underlying method.

### Request Example
```r
open_dataset(
  sources = "path/to/directory",
  schema = NULL,
  partitioning = hive_partition(),
  hive_style = NA,
  unify_schemas = NULL,
  format = "parquet",
  factory_options = list()
)
```

### Response
#### Success Response
Returns a Dataset object representing the opened multi-file dataset.

#### Response Example
```r
# A Dataset object
```
```

### FileFormat$create

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/FileFormat.Rd

Documentation for the FileFormat$create factory method, which creates a FileFormat object for reading and parsing files in a Dataset.

```APIDOC
## FileFormat$create

### Description
Creates a FileFormat object that holds information about how to read and parse files in a Dataset. The factory method returns the appropriate subclass of FileFormat (e.g., ParquetFileFormat) based on the format identifier.

### Method
FileFormat$create()

### Parameters
- **format** (string) - Required - A string identifier of the file format. Supported values: "parquet", "ipc"/"arrow" (also "feather" but deprecated), "csv"/"text" (aliases), "tsv" (equivalent to format = "text", delimiter = "\t").
- **...** - Optional - Additional format-specific options.

#### For format = "parquet":
- **dict_columns** - Names of columns which should be read as dictionaries.
- Any Parquet options from FragmentScanOptions.

#### For format = "text":
- Options from CsvParseOptions (can be specified with Arrow C++ library naming or readr-style naming).
- From CsvReadOptions:
  - **skip_rows**
  - **column_names** - Note: if a Schema is specified, column_names must match those specified in the schema.
  - **autogenerate_column_names**
- From CsvFragmentScanOptions (can be overridden at scan time):
  - **convert_options** - a CsvConvertOptions
  - **block_size**

### Request Example
```r
# Semi-colon delimited files
# Set up directory for examples
tf <- tempfile()
dir.create(tf)
on.exit(unlink(tf))
write.table(mtcars, file.path(tf, "file1.txt"), sep = ";", row.names = FALSE)

# Create FileFormat object
format <- FileFormat$create(format = "text", delimiter = ";")

open_dataset(tf, format = format)
```

### Response
Returns the appropriate subclass of FileFormat (e.g., ParquetFileFormat).
```

### Checking arrow::Result outcome

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/conventions.rst

Shows how to check the outcome of an operation that returns an arrow::Result. The example allocates a buffer and handles the error case by checking the ok() method, then dereferences the result to obtain the buffer.

```cpp
const int64_t buffer_size = 4096;

auto maybe_buffer = arrow::AllocateBuffer(buffer_size, &buffer);
if (!maybe_buffer.ok()) {
   // ... handle error
} else {
   std::shared_ptr<arrow::Buffer> buffer = *maybe_buffer;
   // ... use allocated buffer
}
```

### Skip build phases with --no-pull and --no-build

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/developers/continuous_integration/docker.rst

Use these commands to skip the pull and build phases when the image is already built, to avoid cache misses. The first two runs ensure the image is built, and the third skips the build.

```bash
# first run ensures that the image is built
archery docker run conda-python

# if the second run tries the build the image again and none of the files
# referenced in the relevant dockerfile have changed, then it indicates a
# cache miss caused by the issue described above
archery docker run conda-python

# since the image is properly built with the first command, there is no
# need to rebuild it, so manually disable the pull and build phases to
# spare the some time
archery docker run --no-pull --no-build conda-python
```

### Defining a custom RationalType extension type

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/extending_types.rst

Subclass ExtensionType to define a custom rational type with integer storage. The example shows the required __init__, __arrow_ext_serialize__, and __arrow_ext_deserialize__ methods, including sanity checks on the storage type.

```python
>>> import pyarrow as pa
>>> class RationalType(pa.ExtensionType):
...
...     def __init__(self, data_type: pa.DataType):
...         if not pa.types.is_integer(data_type):
...             raise TypeError(f"data_type must be an integer type not {data_type}")
...
...         super().__init__(
...             pa.struct(
...                 [
...                     ("numer", data_type),
...                     ("denom", data_type),
...                 ],
...             ),
...             "my_package.rational",
...         )
...
...     def __arrow_ext_serialize__(self) -> bytes:
...         # No parameters are necessary
...         return b""
...
...     @classmethod
...     def __arrow_ext_deserialize__(cls, storage_type, serialized):
...         # Sanity checks, not required but illustrate the method signature.
...         assert pa.types.is_struct(storage_type)
...         assert pa.types.is_integer(storage_type[0].type)
...         assert storage_type[0].type == storage_type[1].type
...         assert serialized == b""
...
...         # return an instance of this subclass
...         return RationalType(storage_type[0].type)
```

### Copy CUDA buffer back to host memory

### Use types_mapper with a dtype mapping dictionary

### Python-Java interop with JPype and Arrow C Data

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/integration/python_java.rst

Initializes the JVM with JPype, creates a Python record batch reader, exports it via the C Data interface, and passes it to a Java demo class that writes a JSON file. Then writes an Arrow IPC file for Java to read and imports the result back into Python. Requires the Java demo class and dependencies to be built with Maven.

```python
# Init the JVM and make demo class available to Python.
jpype.startJVM(classpath=["./dependencies/*", "./target/*"])
PythonInteropDemo = JClass("PythonInteropDemo")
demo = PythonInteropDemo()

# Create a Python record batch reader
import pyarrow as pa
schema = pa.schema([
    ("ints", pa.int64()),
    ("strs", pa.string())
])
batches = [
    pa.record_batch([
        [0, 2, 4, 8],
        ["a", "b", "c", None],
    ], schema=schema),
    pa.record_batch([
        [None, 32, 64, None],
        ["e", None, None, "h"],
    ], schema=schema),
]
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_batches(schema, batches)

from pyarrow.cffi import ffi as arrow_c

# Export the Python reader through C Data
c_stream = arrow_c.new("struct ArrowArrayStream*")
c_stream_ptr = int(arrow_c.cast("uintptr_t", c_stream))
reader._export_to_c(c_stream_ptr)

# Send reader to the Java function that writes a JSON file
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as temp:
    demo.importStream(temp.name, c_stream_ptr)

    # Read the JSON file back
    with open(temp.name) as source:
        print("JSON file written by Java:")
        print(source.read())


# Write an Arrow IPC file for Java to read
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as temp:
    with pa.ipc.new_file(temp.name, schema) as sink:
        for batch in batches:
            sink.write_batch(batch)

    demo.exportStream(temp.name, c_stream_ptr)
    with pa.RecordBatchReader._import_from_c(c_stream_ptr) as source:
        print("IPC file read by Java:")
        print(source.read_all())
```

### ArrowAsyncProducer.request

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDeviceDataInterface.rst

A mandatory function that must be called by a consumer to start receiving calls to on_next_task. It must be valid to call synchronously from within on_next_task or on_schema, and must not synchronously call on_next_task or on_error to avoid recursive callbacks.

```APIDOC
## ArrowAsyncProducer.request

### Description
This function must be called by a consumer to start receiving calls to ArrowAsyncDeviceStreamHandler.on_next_task. It must be valid to call this synchronously from within ArrowAsyncDeviceStreamHandler.on_next_task or ArrowAsyncDeviceStreamHandler.on_schema. As a result, this function must not synchronously call on_next_task or on_error to avoid recursive and reentrant callbacks.

### Signature
void (*)(struct ArrowAsyncProducer*, uint64_t)

### Parameters
- **producer** (struct ArrowAsyncProducer*) - The producer object.
- **n** (uint64_t) - The number of additional arrays/batches to be produced. Must be > 0.

### Behavior
- After cancel is called, additional calls to this function must be a NOP, but allowed.
- While not cancelled, calling this function registers the given number of additional arrays/batches to be produced by the producer.
- A producer should only call the appropriate on_next_task callback up to a maximum of the total sum of calls to this method before propagating back-pressure / waiting.
- Any error encountered by calling request must be propagated by calling the on_error callback of the ArrowAsyncDeviceStreamHandler.
- It is invalid to call this function with a value of n that is <= 0. Producers should error (e.g. call on_error) if receiving such a value for n.
```

### Run Jaeger all-in-one Docker container

### Write Feather with compression options (lz4, zstd, uncompressed)

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/feather.rst

Demonstrates compression options for Feather V2 files. LZ4 is the default if available; ZSTD and uncompressed are alternatives. LZ4 generally yields much smaller files without sacrificing much read/write performance.

```python
# Uses LZ4 by default
feather.write_feather(df, file_path)

# Use LZ4 explicitly
feather.write_feather(df, file_path, compression='lz4')

# Use ZSTD
feather.write_feather(df, file_path, compression='zstd')

# Do not compress
feather.write_feather(df, file_path, compression='uncompressed')
```

write_csv_dataset(cars, tf2)

open_csv_dataset(tf2, col_types = schema(speed = int32()))
open_csv_dataset(tf2, col_types = "ii", col_names = c("speed", "dist"), skip = 1)

### pa.array

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/extending_types.rst

Documentation for creating a PyArrow array, with automatic UUID type inference and explicit type specification.

```APIDOC
## pa.array

### Description
Creates a PyArrow array from a sequence of Python objects. When given uuid.UUID objects, PyArrow infers the UUID extension type (arrow.uuid). The UUID type can also be explicitly specified using pa.uuid().

### Method
array

### Parameters
- **obj** (sequence) - Required - The sequence of Python objects to convert.
- **type** (pa.DataType, optional) - Optional - The Arrow type to use. If not provided, it is inferred from the data.

### Returns
- **pa.Array** - A PyArrow array. For uuid.UUID input, returns an array of type UuidType(extension<arrow.uuid>).

### Example
```python
>>> import uuid
>>> import pyarrow as pa
>>> uuids = [uuid.uuid4() for _ in range(3)]
>>> arr = pa.array(uuids)
>>> arr.type
UuidType(extension<arrow.uuid>)
>>> pa.array([uuid.uuid4(), uuid.uuid4()], type=pa.uuid())
<pyarrow.lib.UuidArray object at ...>
```
```

### Define Point3DArray and Point3DType extension classes

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/extending_types.rst

Defines a custom PyArrow extension type for 3D points with a custom array class that adds a to_numpy_array method. The extension type serializes to an empty bytes and deserializes to itself.

```python
>>> class Point3DArray(pa.ExtensionArray):
...     def to_numpy_array(self):
...         return self.storage.flatten().to_numpy().reshape((-1, 3))
>>> class Point3DType(pa.ExtensionType):
...     def __init__(self):
...         super().__init__(pa.list_(pa.float32(), 3), "my_package.Point3DType")
...
...     def __arrow_ext_serialize__(self):
...         return b""
...
...     @classmethod
...     def __arrow_ext_deserialize__(cls, storage_type, serialized):
...         return Point3DType()
...
...     def __arrow_ext_class__(self):
...         return Point3DArray
```

### Export pyarrow array via C Data and call FillTen.fillCArray

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/integration/python_java.rst

Exports a pyarrow array and its schema via the C Data interface and passes the pointers to the Java method FillTen.fillCArray. Requires cffi and a JVM started with the dependencies and target jars.

```python
import jpype
import jpype.imports
from jpype.types import *

# Init the JVM and make FillTen class available to Python.
jpype.startJVM(classpath=["./dependencies/*", "./target/*"])
FillTen = JClass('FillTen')

# Create a Python array of 10 elements
import pyarrow as pa
array = pa.array([0]*10)

from pyarrow.cffi import ffi as arrow_c

# Export the Python array through C Data
c_array = arrow_c.new("struct ArrowArray*")
c_array_ptr = int(arrow_c.cast("uintptr_t", c_array))
array._export_to_c(c_array_ptr)

# Export the Schema of the Array through C Data
c_schema = arrow_c.new("struct ArrowSchema*")
c_schema_ptr = int(arrow_c.cast("uintptr_t", c_schema))
array.type._export_to_c(c_schema_ptr)

# Send Array and its Schema to the Java function
# that will populate the array with numbers from 1 to 10
FillTen.fillCArray(c_array_ptr, c_schema_ptr)

# See how the content of our Python array was changed from Java
# while it remained of the Python type.
print("ARRAY", type(array), array)
```

### Execute Substrait Query with PyArrow Dataset Scanner

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/integration/substrait.rst

Use pyarrow.dataset and pyarrow.substrait to execute a Substrait Extended Expression against a dataset. The example shows how to create a projection and filter expression, merge them with the schema, and pass them to the scanner.

```python
>>> import pyarrow.dataset as ds  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> # Use substrait-python to create the queries
>>> from substrait import proto  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> dataset = ds.dataset("./data/index-0.parquet")  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> substrait_schema = pa_substrait.serialize_schema(dataset.schema).to_pysubstrait()  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> # SELECT project_name FROM dataset WHERE project_name = 'pyarrow'
>>> projection = proto.ExtendedExpression(referred_expr=[  # doctest: +SKIP
...     {"expression": {"selection": {"direct_reference": {"struct_field": {"field": 0}}}}},
...     "output_names": ["project_name"]}
... ])
>>> projection.MergeFrom(substrait_schema)  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> filtering = proto.ExtendedExpression(  # doctest: +SKIP
...         extension_uris=[{"extension_uri_anchor": 99, "uri": "/functions_comparison.yaml"}],
...         extensions=[{"extension_function": {"extension_uri_reference": 99, "function_anchor": 199, "name": "equal:any1_any1"}}],
...         referred_expr=[
...             {"expression": {"scalar_function": {"function_reference": 199, "arguments": [
...                 {"value": {"selection": {"direct_reference": {"struct_field": {"field": 0}}}}},
...                 {"value": {"literal": {"string": "pyarrow"}}}
...             ], "output_type": {"bool": {"nullability": False}}}}}
...         ]
... )
>>> filtering.MergeFrom(substrait_schema)  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> results = dataset.scanner(  # doctest: +SKIP
...     columns=pa.substrait.BoundExpressions.from_substrait(projection),
...     filter=pa.substrait.BoundExpressions.from_substrait(filtering)
... ).head(5)
```

### New import method supporting PyCapsule interface

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.rst

Rewritten import method that prefers the __arrow_c_array__ method for newer PyArrow versions and falls back to the deprecated _export_to_c for older versions. Raises a TypeError for unsupported types.

```python
# NEW METHOD
def from_arrow(arr)
    # Newer versions of PyArrow as well as other libraries with Arrow data
    # implement this method, so prefer it over _export_to_c.
    if hasattr(arr, "__arrow_c_array__"):
         schema_ptr, array_ptr = arr.__arrow_c_array__()
         return import_c_capsule_data(schema_ptr, array_ptr)
    elif isinstance(arr, pa.Array):
         # Deprecated method, used for older versions of PyArrow
         array_import_ptr = make_array_import_ptr()
         schema_import_ptr = make_schema_import_ptr()
         arr._export_to_c(array_import_ptr, schema_import_ptr)
         return import_c_data(array_import_ptr, schema_import_ptr)
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"Cannot import {type(arr)} as Arrow array data.")
```

### pyarrow.substrait API

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/integration/substrait.rst

Code examples for the pyarrow.substrait module functions for schema and expression serialization/deserialization.

```APIDOC
## pyarrow.substrait.serialize_schema

### Description
Encodes an Arrow schema into a Substrait representation. Returns an object with the marshalled schema and expression.

### Method
serialize_schema

### Parameters
- **schema** (pyarrow.Schema) - Required - The Arrow schema to serialize.

### Returns
- **substrait_schema** (object) - Contains `schema` (Substrait NamedStruct) and `expression` (Extended Expression) attributes.

### Example
```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait
arrow_schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.string())
])
substrait_schema = pa_substrait.serialize_schema(arrow_schema)
print(bytes(substrait_schema.schema))
print(bytes(substrait_schema.expression))
```
```

```APIDOC
## pyarrow.substrait.deserialize_schema

### Description
Decodes a Substrait representation back into an Arrow schema.

### Method
deserialize_schema

### Parameters
- **substrait_schema** (object) - Required - The Substrait schema object to deserialize.

### Returns
- **arrow_schema** (pyarrow.Schema) - The decoded Arrow schema.

### Example
```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait
arrow_schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.string())
])
substrait_schema = pa_substrait.serialize_schema(arrow_schema)
decoded_schema = pa_substrait.deserialize_schema(substrait_schema)
```
```

```APIDOC
## pyarrow.substrait.serialize_expressions

### Description
Encodes Arrow compute expressions into a Substrait ExtendedExpression message.

### Method
serialize_expressions

### Parameters
- **exprs** (list of pyarrow.compute.Expression) - Required - The expressions to serialize.
- **names** (list of str) - Required - Names for the output fields.
- **schema** (pyarrow.Schema) - Required - The Arrow schema for the expressions.

### Returns
- **substrait_expr** (bytes) - The protobuf ExtendedExpression message data.

### Example
```python
import pyarrow.compute as pc
arrow_schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.int32())
])
substrait_expr = pa_substrait.serialize_expressions(
    exprs=[pc.field("x") + pc.field("y")],
    names=["total"],
    schema=arrow_schema
)
print(bytes(substrait_expr))
```
```

```APIDOC
## pyarrow.substrait.deserialize_expressions

### Description
Decodes a Substrait ExtendedExpression message back into Arrow compute expressions.

### Method
deserialize_expressions

### Parameters
- **substrait_expr** (bytes) - Required - The Substrait ExtendedExpression message data.

### Returns
- **exprs** (list of pyarrow.compute.Expression) - The decoded Arrow expressions.

### Example
```python
import pyarrow.compute as pc
arrow_schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.int32())
])
substrait_expr = pa_substrait.serialize_expressions(
    exprs=[pc.field("x") + pc.field("y")],
    names=["total"],
    schema=arrow_schema
)
decoded_exprs = pa_substrait.deserialize_expressions(substrait_expr)
```

### schema(...)

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/schema.Rd

Creates a schema from field name/data type pairs, a list of such pairs, or field objects. It can also extract a schema from an object that has one, such as an Arrow table.

```APIDOC
## schema(...)

### Description
Creates a schema from field name/data type pairs, a list of such pairs, or field objects. It can also extract a schema from an object that has one, such as an Arrow table.

### Usage
schema(...)

### Arguments
- **...** - Fields, field name/data type pairs (or a list of), or object from which to extract a schema.

### Examples
```r
# Create schema using pairs of field names and data types
schema(a = int32(), b = float64())

# Create a schema using a list of pairs of field names and data types
schema(list(a = int8(), b = string()))

# Create schema using fields
schema(
  field("b", double()),
  field("c", bool(), nullable = FALSE),
  field("d", string())
)

# Extract schemas from objects
df <- data.frame(col1 = 2:4, col2 = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5))
tab1 <- arrow_table(df)
schema(tab1)
tab2 <- arrow_table(df, schema = schema(col1 = int8(), col2 = float32()))
schema(tab2)

### Export struct<float32, utf8> type as ArrowSchema

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDataInterface.rst

Exports a struct<float32, utf8> type as an ArrowSchema with C-malloc()ed children. The release callback frees child schemas and the children array, then marks the schema as released. The parent schema uses format "+s" with two children: "f" for floats and "u" for strings, both flagged ARROW_FLAG_NULLABLE.

```c
static void release_malloced_type(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
   int i;
   for (i = 0; i < schema->n_children; ++i) {
      struct ArrowSchema* child = schema->children[i];
      if (child->release != NULL) {
         child->release(child);
      }
      free(child);
   }
   free(schema->children);
   // Mark released
   schema->release = NULL;
}

void export_float32_utf8_type(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
   struct ArrowSchema* child;

   //
   // Initialize parent type
   //
   *schema = (struct ArrowSchema) {
      // Type description
      .format = "+s",
      .name = "",
      .metadata = NULL,
      .flags = 0,
      .n_children = 2,
      .dictionary = NULL,
      // Bookkeeping
      .release = &release_malloced_type
   };
   // Allocate list of children types
   schema->children = malloc(sizeof(struct ArrowSchema*) * schema->n_children);

   //
   // Initialize child type #0
   //
   child = schema->children[0] = malloc(sizeof(struct ArrowSchema));
   *child = (struct ArrowSchema) {
      // Type description
      .format = "f",
      .name = "floats",
      .metadata = NULL,
      .flags = ARROW_FLAG_NULLABLE,
      .n_children = 0,
      .dictionary = NULL,
      .children = NULL,
      // Bookkeeping
      .release = &release_malloced_type
   };

   //
   // Initialize child type #1
   //
   child = schema->children[1] = malloc(sizeof(struct ArrowSchema));
   *child = (struct ArrowSchema) {
      // Type description
      .format = "u",
      .name = "strings",
      .metadata = NULL,
      .flags = ARROW_FLAG_NULLABLE,
      .n_children = 0,
      .dictionary = NULL,
      .children = NULL,
      // Bookkeeping
      .release = &release_malloced_type
   };
}
```

### Producing: Convert PyArrow FixedShapeTensorArray to NumPy array

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/dlpack.rst

Convert a PyArrow FixedShapeTensorArray directly to a NumPy array using the DLPack protocol.

```APIDOC
## [Producing] Convert PyArrow FixedShapeTensorArray to NumPy array

### Description
Convert a PyArrow FixedShapeTensorArray directly to a NumPy array using the DLPack protocol.

### Method
Producing

### Endpoint
np.from_dlpack(tensor_array)

### Parameters
- **tensor_array** (pyarrow.FixedShapeTensorArray) - Required - The PyArrow FixedShapeTensorArray to convert.

### Request Example
```python
import pyarrow as pa
import numpy as np
nested = pa.array([[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]], pa.list_(pa.list_(pa.int32(), 2), 2))
tensor_array = pa.FixedShapeTensorArray.from_tensor(nested.to_tensor())
np.from_dlpack(tensor_array)
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **result** (numpy.ndarray) - The converted NumPy array with shape (array_length, *element_shape).

#### Response Example
```python
array shape: (2, 2, 2)
```
```

### Implementing __arrow_array__ on a duck array class

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/extending_types.rst

Define the __arrow_array__ method on a custom array-like class to enable conversion to a PyArrow Array via pyarrow.array. The method receives an optional type keyword passed through from pyarrow.array and should return an Arrow Array or ChunkedArray.

```python
>>> class MyDuckArray:
...
...     def __arrow_array__(self, type=None):
...         # convert the underlying array values to a PyArrow Array
...         import pyarrow
...         return pyarrow.array(..., type=type)
```

### Define a Schema with Fields in Arrow C++

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/cpp/tutorials/basic_arrow.rst

Defines a Schema for a RecordBatch by creating Field objects with names and data types (int8 for Day and Month, int16 for Year) and grouping them into a Schema. This is the first step before constructing a RecordBatch.

```cpp
  // Now, we want a RecordBatch, which has columns and labels for said columns.
  // This gets us to the 2d data structures we want in Arrow.
  // These are defined by schema, which have fields -- here we get both those object types
  // ready.
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Field> field_day, field_month, field_year;
  std::shared_ptr<arrow::Schema> schema;

  // Every field needs its name and data type.
  field_day = arrow::field("Day", arrow::int8());
  field_month = arrow::field("Month", arrow::int8());
  field_year = arrow::field("Year", arrow::int16());

  // The schema can be built from a vector of fields, and we do so here.
  schema = arrow::schema({field_day, field_month, field_year});
```

### int import_pyarrow()

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/integration/extending.rst

Initializes inner pointers of the pyarrow API. Must be called before any other pyarrow C++ API function.

```APIDOC
## int import_pyarrow()

### Description
Initialize inner pointers of the pyarrow API. On success, 0 is returned. Otherwise, -1 is returned and a Python exception is set. It is mandatory to call this function before calling any other function in the pyarrow C++ API.

### Method
C++ function

### Signature
`int import_pyarrow()`

### Parameters
None

### Return Value
- **int** - 0 on success, -1 on failure (Python exception set).

### Usage Example
cpp
#include <arrow/python/pyarrow.h>

if (import_pyarrow() != 0) {
    // handle error
}

```

### Producing: Convert PyArrow array with nulls to NumPy array

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/dlpack.rst

Convert a PyArrow array with nulls to a NumPy array using the DLPack protocol, with optional allow_nulls.

```APIDOC
## [Producing] Convert PyArrow array with nulls to NumPy array

### Description
Convert a PyArrow array with nulls to a NumPy array using the DLPack protocol. Arrays with nulls are rejected unless the conversion to a tensor explicitly allows them.

### Method
Producing

### Endpoint
np.from_dlpack(array) or np.from_dlpack(array.to_tensor(allow_nulls=True))

### Parameters
- **array** (pyarrow.Array) - Required - The PyArrow array with nulls.
- **allow_nulls** (bool) - Optional - When using to_tensor, set to True to allow nulls; null entries hold an unspecified value.

### Request Example
```python
import pyarrow as pa
import numpy as np
array_with_nulls = pa.array([2, None, 4], pa.int32())
# This raises an error:
# np.from_dlpack(array_with_nulls)
# This works:
np.from_dlpack(array_with_nulls.to_tensor(allow_nulls=True))
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **result** (numpy.ndarray) - The converted NumPy array with null entries holding an unspecified value.

#### Response Example
```python
array([2, ..., 4], dtype=int32)
```

#### Error Response
- **pyarrow.lib.ArrowTypeError** - Raised when attempting to use DLPack on arrays with nulls without allow_nulls=True.
```

### Use types_mapper to convert Arrow int64 to pandas Int64

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/pandas.rst

Shows how to use the types_mapper keyword of pyarrow.Table.to_pandas to override the default pandas dtype. Here, it maps pa.int64() to pd.Int64Dtype(), producing a nullable Int64 column instead of float64.

```python
>>> table = pa.table({"a": [1, 2, None]})
>>> table.to_pandas()
     a
0  1.0
1  2.0
2  NaN
>>> table.to_pandas(types_mapper={pa.int64(): pd.Int64Dtype()}.get)
      a
0     1
1     2
2  <NA>
```

### Parse timestamps with time zones using schema

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/r/man/read_delim_arrow.Rd

The string 'T' col_types specification does not handle time zones. Provide a Schema with the timezone specified in the timestamp type.

```R
tf <- tempfile()
write.csv(data.frame(x = "1970-01-01T12:00:00+12:00"), file = tf, row.names = FALSE)
read_csv_arrow(
  tf,
  col_types = schema(x = timestamp(unit = "us", timezone = "UTC"))
)
```

### write_table

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/python/orc.rst

Writes a PyArrow table to an ORC file with options for file version, stripe size, compression, and filesystem.

```APIDOC
## write_table

### Description
Writes a PyArrow table to an ORC file with configurable options.

### Parameters
- **table** (Table) - The table to write.
- **where** (str or file-like) - The destination path or file object.
- **file_version** (str, optional) - ORC format version: `'0.11'` or `'0.12'`. Default is `'0.12'`.
- **stripe_size** (int, optional) - Approximate size of data within a column stripe. Default is 64MB.
- **compression** (str, optional) - Compression codec: `'uncompressed'`, `'zlib'`, `'zstd'`, `'snappy'`, or `'lz4'`. Default is `'uncompressed'`.
- **filesystem** (FileSystem, optional) - Filesystem to use for non-local paths.

### Usage Examples
```python
>>> orc.write_table(table, 'example.orc', compression='uncompressed')
>>> orc.write_table(table, 'example.orc', compression='zlib')
>>> orc.write_table(table, 'example.orc', compression='zstd')
>>> orc.write_table(table, 'example.orc', compression='snappy')
```
```

### Export int32 ArrowSchema with trivial release callback

Source: https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/main/docs/source/format/CDataInterface.rst

Exports a non-nullable int32 type with empty metadata. All ArrowSchema members point to statically-allocated data, so the release callback is trivial and only marks the schema as released.

```c
static void release_int32_type(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
   // Mark released
   schema->release = NULL;
}

void export_int32_type(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
   *schema = (struct ArrowSchema) {
      // Type description
      .format = "i",
      .name = "",
      .metadata = NULL,
      .flags = 0,
      .n_children = 0,
      .children = NULL,
      .dictionary = NULL,
      // Bookkeeping
      .release = &release_int32_type
   };
}
```
